subcomponents.title: Uses scene-kit APIs without bypassing or duplicating them

criteria.rationale: The Talk renders the kit's `Presentation` and builds steps with the kit's `defineStep`. The shared Scene is built from kit primitives and does not re-implement them. `Presentation` hands each step to the kit's `Stage`, which renders `step.render()` inside `LayoutGroup` and `AnimatePresence`. Entity morphing and grouping therefore come from the kit.
evidence: Talk.tsx returns `<Presentation className="htmp" steps={STEPS} title=... initialMode="browse" />`, imported from '../../presentation-kit'.
steps/index.ts maps OUTLINE through `defineStep({ ...beat, Scene: SampleScene, groupKey: 'scene', payload: { stage: index + 1 } })`.
steps/scene.tsx: `SampleScene({ payload }: SceneProps<SamplePayload>)` renders kit `SceneLayer`, `Presence` and `Appear`.
steps/layout.tsx and steps/parts.tsx build entities from kit `Box`, `Label`, `Arrow`, `Emphasis`, `Frame` and `SymbolChip`.
The nodes (`Box`, `Label`, `Frame`, `Emphasis`, `SymbolChip`) delegate to the kit's `EntityNode` (`motion.div` with `layout` and `layoutId={id}`). I did not trace `Arrow`'s own path animation…
Stage.tsx wraps `step.render()` in `LayoutGroup` and `AnimatePresence`, keyed by the kit's `hostKey(step)`.

subcomponents.title: Uses stable identities and appropriate grouped-scene architecture

criteria.rationale: Grouping: steps/index.ts builds all nine steps from one OUTLINE.map call with the same Scene (SampleScene) and groupKey 'scene'. defineStep (steps.ts) gives every step the same sceneId, and hostKey returns the identical 'group:scene:<sceneId>' for all nine. Stage.tsx keys a single motion.div on hostKey(step) and renders step.render() inside it. Presentation.tsx passes the current step to Stage. Navigating between any two steps therefore keeps the same host key and the same mounted SampleScene, which only receives a new payload.stage. That is an in-place update, not a remount. A single shared groupKey is correct for this one continuously evolving scene. Identity: entities.ts defines the presentation-owned E constants (29 members). layout.tsx passes each as id={E.x} to Box, Label, SymbolChip, Frame, Emphasis and Arrow, and also as the React key. The StepCard and Morph helpers in parts.tsx forward their id to Box and SymbolChip. Box, Label, SymbolChip, Frame and Emphasis each render EntityNode with a kind and the props. EntityNode renders motion.div with layout and layoutId={id}, plus data-presentation-entity={id}. Stage wraps the scene in LayoutGroup. Arrow takes the same id as data-presentation-entity and animates its path from the one remembered in ArrowMemoryContext, which Stage provides. Every E member is consumed by a rendered element in layout.tsx, directly or via parts.tsx. SampleScene filters SAMPLE_ENTITIES by stage, so each entity keeps the same key and id from its first beat on. Presence and Appear are keyed wrappers and don't change identity. Entities that persist across consecutive steps share a layoutId and morph in place.
evidence: steps/index.ts: STEPS = OUTLINE.map(... defineStep({ ...beat, Scene: SampleScene, groupKey: 'scene', payload: { stage: index + 1 } })) covers all nine OUTLINE beats, each with the same Scene …

Stage.tsx: <motion.div key={hostKey(step)}>{step.render()}</motion.div> inside AnimatePresence and LayoutGroup. One host key means one mounted scene instance.
scene.tsx: SampleScene renders SAMPLE_ENTITIES.filter(entity.from <= payload.stage) with key={entity.key} inside Presence and Appear. Only the stage payload changes between steps.
layout.tsx: every entry passes id={E.*} (and key: E.*) to Box, Label, Arrow, SymbolChip, Emphasis or Frame, or to StepCard and Morph. All 29 E members are used.
parts.tsx: StepCard forwards id to Box and Morph forwards id to SymbolChip.
Box.tsx, Label.tsx, SymbolChip.tsx, Frame.tsx and Emphasis.tsx each return <EntityNode kind=... {...props} />.

subcomponents.title: Verification tooling robustness

criteria.rationale: Both the repo and bootstrap copies start the preview as `node vite.js preview`, not through an npm wrapper. The child is spawned detached and registered in `children`. `stopAll()` SIGTERMs the whole process group, polls until each child's exit code or signal is set, and escalates to SIGKILL. Every exit path reaches it. In verify.mjs, `main()` calls `stopAll()` in a `finally`, which covers success, check failures, a `chromium.launch()` failure inside `renderSample`, and errors after the preview started. In inspect-presentation.mjs, the outer `try/catch/finally` calls `stopAll()` and then `process.exit`. Signal handlers also call `stopAll`. The runtime.mjs files are identical in both locations.
evidence: runtime.mjs `startPreview` spawns `process.execPath [vite.js preview ...]` with `detached: true` and adds the child to `children`.
`stopAll` sends `process.kill(-pid, 'SIGTERM')`, waits on `exitCode`/`signalCode`, and escalates to SIGKILL after 3s.
verify.mjs `main()` has `finally { await stopAll() }`; inspect-presentation.mjs has `finally { await stopAll() }` before `process.exit(code)`.
The bootstrap template copies of verify.mjs, inspect-presentation.mjs and lib/runtime.mjs are identical to the repo copies.
judging basis: consensus-pass

criteria.rationale: All three clauses are met. The readiness loop in `startPreview` has a 30s deadline and also fails if the child exits. The follow-up wait for the printed URL is capped at 20 iterations. verify.mjs awaits `build()` (`runNpm('build')`) in its own phase before `renderSample` starts the preview. inspect awaits the build before `startPreview`, and skips it only with `--no-build`. Readiness itself is an HTTP probe via `fetch`. The printed URL is only used to report the bound address. It is parsed from the accumulated output buffer after stripping ANSI codes, so it tolerates colour codes and chunk splits.
evidence: `startPreview`: `deadline = Date.now() + 30_000`, with a throw on timeout and on early exit.
`output` accumulates across chunks, `stripAnsi` runs on the whole buffer, and the wait loop is bounded to `wait < 20`.
verify `main()` runs `phase='build'; await build()` before `renderSample`.
inspect awaits `runNpm('build')` before `startPreview()` when `options.build` is true.
judging basis: consensus-pass

criteria.rationale: The template verify.mjs does not verify every registered route or take a target from an argument. It checks only the single `reference` read from scripts/verify.config.json, whose slug is `starter` with two hardcoded steps. Every other registered slug gets only a first-step render. Because the reference never changes, verify keeps checking the hardcoded starter route even after the agent adds its own presentation. The template inspect.mjs does take a slug argument, but an unregistered slug is not rejected clearly. The slug is only checked against a format regex, then the script waits up to 5s for `[data-step-count]` and fails with a render timeout. It never consults the registry.
evidence: The template verify.config.json embeds `slug: "starter"` and the titles 'Replace this opening beat' and 'Replace this second beat'.
The template verify.mjs `loadReference()` reads only that config, and `checkSampleRegistration` and `renderSample` assert only that reference.
The template inspect `parseArgs` only requires a slug; unknown slugs go through `waitForSelector('[data-step-count]', {timeout: 5000})`, which throws 'did not render a presentation'.
judging basis: consensus-fail

criteria.rationale: The inspect helper does not satisfy the first and third clauses. It reads `count = Number(getAttribute('data-step-count'))` with no validation. A missing or non-numeric attribute gives NaN or 0, the `for (index < count)` loop never runs, and the script prints 'done: 0 screenshots' and exits 0. That is success with zero captures. It also never rejects a zero or non-numeric step index. It confirms the index only through `waitForFunction` for steps after the first. votes.rationale: Grouping: steps/index.ts builds all nine steps from one OUTLINE.map call with the same Scene (SampleScene) and groupKey 'scene'. defineStep (steps.ts) gives every step the same sceneId, and hostKey returns the identical 'group:scene:<sceneId>' for all nine. Stage.tsx keys a single motion.div on hostKey(step) and renders step.render() inside it. Presentation.tsx passes the current step to Stage. Navigating between any two steps therefore keeps the same host key and the same mounted SampleScene, which only receives a new payload.stage. That is an in-place update, not a remount. A single shared groupKey is correct for this one continuously evolving scene. Identity: entities.ts defines the presentation-owned E constants (29 members). layout.tsx passes each as id={E.x} to Box, Label, SymbolChip, Frame, Emphasis and Arrow, and also as the React key. The StepCard and Morph helpers in parts.tsx forward their id to Box and SymbolChip. Box, Label, SymbolChip, Frame and Emphasis each render EntityNode with a kind and the props. EntityNode renders motion.div with layout and layoutId={id}, plus data-presentation-entity={id}. Stage wraps the scene in LayoutGroup. Arrow takes the same id as data-presentation-entity and animates its path from the one remembered in ArrowMemoryContext, which Stage provides. Every E member is consumed by a rendered element in layout.tsx, directly or via parts.tsx. SampleScene filters SAMPLE_ENTITIES by stage, so each entity keeps the same key and id from its first beat on. Presence and Appear are keyed wrappers and don't change identity. Entities that persist across consecutive steps share a layoutId and morph in place.

votes.rationale: Readiness comes from HTTP-polling the probe URL, not from the child's own announcement of its address. The only ownership check is the `exited` flag, read at the top of each poll iteration, before the fetch. A stale server already listening on the port could answer before the child's exit is observed. VERIFY_PORT also allows a fixed or reused port. The ephemeral port from freePort is released before the child binds it, and --strictPort alone is insufficient. The 'Local:' URL is read only after readiness, so it is not a readiness source.

freePort closes its server before the preview is spawned
verify.mjs only checks that the reported boundUrl host is 127.0.0.1, not that the port or process matches

votes.rationale: Both the repo and bootstrap copies start the preview as `node vite.js preview`, not through an npm wrapper. The child is spawned detached and registered in `children`. `stopAll()` SIGTERMs the whole process group, polls until each child's exit code or signal is set, and escalates to SIGKILL. Every exit path reaches it. In verify.mjs, `main()` calls `stopAll()` in a `finally`, which covers success, check failures, a `chromium.launch()` failure inside `renderSample`, and errors after the preview started. In inspect-presentation.mjs, the outer `try/catch/finally` calls `stopAll()` and then `process.exit`. Signal handlers also call `stopAll`. The runtime.mjs files are identical in both locations.
evidence: runtime.mjs `startPreview` spawns `process.execPath [vite.js preview ...]` with `detached: true` and adds the child to `children`.
`stopAll` sends `process.kill(-pid, 'SIGTERM')`, waits on `exitCode`/`signalCode`, and escalates to SIGKILL after 3s.
verify.mjs `main()` has `finally { await stopAll() }`; inspect-presentation.mjs has `finally { await stopAll() }` before `process.exit(code)`.
The bootstrap template copies of verify.mjs, inspect-presentation.mjs and lib/runtime.mjs are identical to the repo copies.

checks.rationale: The auditor's observation is accurate but does not defeat the pass. On every exit path the guidance names (success, failing check, browser launch failure, error after the preview started), all four entry scripts reach `await stopAll()` in an outer finally. stopAll sends SIGTERM to the detached Vite process group: the server itself, spawned via process.execPath, not an npm or npx wrapper. It then polls until exitCode or signalCode is set, so the exit is awaited. The SIGKILL branch without a further await runs only if Vite ignores SIGTERM for 3 seconds. That is a hypothetical the guidance does not name and the evidence does not show. Even in that case SIGKILL, which cannot be ignored, goes to the server's own process group, so the server does not keep running. None of the guidance's fail conditions applies: a wrapper-only kill, a preview left running after a launch failure or later error, or a copy lacking cleanup.

votes.rationale: The identity-hook clause is unmet. `EntityNode` (used by Box, Label, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip) sets `layoutId`, `data-presentation-entity` and `data-presentation-node` before `{...rest}`. A caller-supplied `data-presentation-entity` or `data-presentation-node` therefore overrides the kit's hook. `Arrow` puts `{...rest}` after `data-presentation-entity` and `data-presentation-node` for the same reason. `Arrow` also types its props as a bespoke `ArrowProps` that does not extend the rendered svg element's props, so `rest` is effectively empty. `Appear` also spreads `{...rest}` after `data-presentation-appear`.

demo-integration.rationale: The packet supports the pass for both fixture scenarios and contains every file in the proof chain. Grouping: all nine steps come from one OUTLINE.map in steps/index.ts, with the same SampleScene and groupKey 'scene'. defineStep gives them one sceneId, so hostKey returns the same group:scene:<id> for all of them. Stage.tsx keys a single motion.div on hostKey(step) and renders step.render() inside it, so moving between steps keeps the same mounted scene and only payload.stage changes. That is an in-place update, and one shared groupKey is correct for this single evolving scene. audit_results.rationale: The criterion passes only when every selector in a stylesheet a presentation owns is "scoped under that presentation's own root class or hook" or comes from a CSS module. The sample's style.css meets this: every selector it quotes, kit-hook rules included, starts with `.htmp`, and Talk.tsx renders `<Presentation className="htmp">`. The two template stylesheets do not meet it. Each has exactly one rule, and that rule is a top-level class selector: `.__SLUG__-box { … }` and `.starter-box { … }`. Neither is nested under a root class or hook, and neither file is a CSS module. The comments in those same files show the root scope this kit expects: `.__SLUG__ [data-presentation-…]` and `.starter [data-presentation-…]`. So the presentation's root class is `.__SLUG__` / `.starter`, and the `-box` rules are outside it. The claim says a slug-prefixed class counts as the presentation's own hook. But that is a naming convention, not scoping under the root. A plain `.starter-box` selector matches any element with that class anywhere in the document, which is exactly the kind of unscoped rule the requirement fails. The quoted lines therefore show that not every presentation-owned selector is scoped, so the pass claim is contradicted.

On every exit path the guidance names (success, failing check, browser launch failure, error after the preview started), all four entry scripts reach `await stopAll()` in an outer finally. stopAll sends SIGTERM to the detached Vite process group: the server itself, spawned via process.execPath, not an npm or npx wrapper. That is a hypothetical the guidance does not name and the evidence does not show. Even in that case SIGKILL, which cannot be ignored, goes to the server's own process group, so the server does not keep running. None of the guidance's fail conditions applies: a wrapper-only kill, a preview left running after a launch failure or later error, or a copy lacking cleanup.
